title: Thread pool deadlock — parent join()s child in same pool, pool segregation fix, virtual threads

s1_definition.profdef: When a "parent" task submits a "child" task to the SAME thread pool and then calls `child.join()`/`child.get()`, the parent thread BLOCKS while holding a pool worker. If ALL workers are occupied by parents waiting for children, NO worker is available for children to execute → **pool deadlock/livelock**: all threads blocked, zero progress. Example: pool of 10, 10 parent tasks each submit a child and `join()` → 10 workers blocked → 10 children queued → children can never run → deadlock! Fix: (1) **Pool segregation** — parents on pool-A, children on pool-B. (2) **Bulkhead** — separate pools per workload. (3) **Virtual threads** (Java 21) — millions of lightweight threads → no finite pool → parent blocks but JVM unmounts it → carrier free for children!
s1_definition.analogy: 10 tellers (pool=10). Each teller (parent) takes a customer form → sends a sub-form to the back office (child task) → WAITS at the counter for the back office reply. Problem: the back office uses the SAME 10 tellers! All 10 tellers waiting → nobody available for back office work → DEADLOCK! Fix: separate front office (10 tellers) and back office (5 clerks). Or: virtual threads → unlimited freelancers, waiting is free!
s1_definition.oneliner: Parent join()s child in same pool → all workers blocked waiting → children can't run → DEADLOCK! Fix: separate pools (parent pool + child pool). Virtual threads: blocking is free → no pool deadlock.
s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** When a "parent" task submits a "child" task to the SAME thread pool and then calls `child.join()`/`child.get()`, the parent thread BLOCKS while holding a pool worker. If ALL workers are occupied by parents waiting for children, NO worker is available for children to execute → **pool deadlock/livelock**: all threads blocked, zero progress. Example: pool of 10, 10 parent tasks each submit a child and `join()` → 10 workers blocked → 10 children queued → children can never run → deadlock! Fix: (1) **Pool segregation** — parents on pool-A, children on pool-B. (2) **Bulkhead** — separate pools per workload. (3) **Virtual threads** (Java 21) — millions of lightweight threads → no finite pool → parent blocks but JVM unmounts it → carrier free for children!

**In simple words (banking analogy):** 10 tellers (pool=10). Each teller (parent) takes a customer form → sends a sub-form to the back office (child task) → WAITS at the counter for the back office reply. Problem: the back office uses the SAME 10 tellers! All 10 tellers waiting → nobody available for back office work → DEADLOCK! Fix: separate front office (10 tellers) and back office (5 clerks). Or: virtual threads → unlimited freelancers, waiting is free!

**One line to remember:** Parent join()s child in same pool → all workers blocked waiting → children can't run → DEADLOCK! Fix: separate pools (parent pool + child pool). Virtual threads: blocking is free → no pool deadlock.

sections.s3_banking: **Problem — The loan approval service had a 10-thread pool.** Each loan request (parent): submitted 3 sub-tasks (credit check, property check, income check) to the SAME pool → `Future.get()`. During peak: 10 loan requests → 10 workers occupied as parents → 30 child tasks queued → no workers for children → DEADLOCK! All 10 requests hung forever. Fix: parentPool(10) for loan requests + childPool(20) for checks. Or: CompletableFuture chain (non-blocking, no join). Or: Java 21 virtual threads.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1 (deadlock).** Pool(2). Parent-1 submits child-1 to SAME pool → blocks on `get()`. Parent-2 submits child-2 → blocks. Both workers occupied by parents. Children queued. Nobody to execute children → DEADLOCK!

**Step 2 (separate pools).** Parent-1 on parentPool → submits child to childPool → childPool worker executes child → result returned → parent continues. No deadlock!

**Step 3 (CF non-blocking).** `thenApplyAsync()` chains stages. Parent's thread freed after submitting. Child stage picks up a free worker. No thread blocks waiting → no deadlock.

**Step 4 (virtual).** 100 parents + 100 children = 200 virtual threads on ~4 carriers. Parent blocks → unmounts → carrier runs child → child completes → parent remounts. No finite pool constraint!
sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ POOL DEADLOCK (same pool) ═══

  Pool(4 workers):
  W1: parent-1 → submit child-1 → child.get() → BLOCKED!
  W2: parent-2 → submit child-2 → child.get() → BLOCKED!
  W3: parent-3 → submit child-3 → child.get() → BLOCKED!
  W4: parent-4 → submit child-4 → child.get() → BLOCKED!
  Queue: [child-1, child-2, child-3, child-4] → NO worker available! DEADLOCK!

  ═══ FIX: SEPARATE POOLS ═══
  parentPool(4): W1-W4 run parents → block on child.get()
  childPool(4):  W5-W8 run children → complete → parents unblock!
  No deadlock! Children always have dedicated workers!

  ═══ FIX: VIRTUAL THREADS ═══
  Virtual threads: blocking = FREE (unmount from carrier)
  Parent blocks → carrier free → child runs → completes → parent resumes
  No finite pool → no deadlock!
```

sections.s5d_lld:
```
  ═══ LLD — Pool Deadlock Mechanism ═══

  Root cause: finite resource (thread) held while waiting
  for a task that NEEDS that same finite resource!

  parent.get() → blocks thread (occupies 1 of N workers)
  child queued → needs a worker → all N workers blocked by parents!
  → classic resource exhaustion → deadlock!

  ═══ THREE FIXES ═══

  1. Pool segregation:
     parentPool(N) + childPool(M) → independent resources!
     Children: dedicated workers → always execute!

  2. Non-blocking (CompletableFuture):
     thenCompose/thenApply → no thread holds → no block → no deadlock!
     Thread freed between stages!

  3. Virtual threads (Java 21):
     parent.get() → unmount virtual thread → carrier FREE!
     child runs on freed carrier → completes → parent remounts!
     No finite pool constraint!
```
sections.s6_takeaway:
Running parent tasks and their child tasks in the SAME bounded pool causes deadlock: all workers become parents blocked on `child.get()`, no worker available to execute children → permanent hang. This is a resource exhaustion deadlock — threads are finite resources held by parents while waiting for children that need those same resources. Three fixes: (1) Pool segregation — parents on pool-A, children on pool-B (bulkhead pattern). (2) Non-blocking pipelines — `CompletableFuture.thenCompose()` instead of `submit() + get()` → no thread blocks. (3) Virtual threads (Java 21) — blocking unmounts the virtual thread from its carrier → carrier free for children → no finite pool constraint.

In banking: loan approval with 10-thread pool → each parent submits 3 children (credit, property, income) to same pool → `get()` → 10 parents block → 30 children queued → deadlock. Fix: parentPool(10) + childPool(20). Or: CompletableFuture chain (non-blocking). Or: virtual threads (Java 21, blocking is free).
